Have a "Need For Speed?" Fond of racing like in Initial D? Did you enjoy the Podrace scene the best in The [[Phantom]] Menance? The characteristics of this famous podracer is well represented in the game text. It maybe not be the fastest of all the podracers, but it is incredibly good at catching up (i.e. getting to choose two racing destinies) when you are losing the podrace -- which is almost always the case since the [[Sebulba]] has a few tricks to get a good start! Being able to pick and choose your destiny is very handy especially at the beginning of the game since you have not had the opportunity to setup your destiny draws yet. The last aspect of [[Anakin's Podracer]] is that you can take the [[I Did It!]] epic event into hand. So instead of a 12 card swing from the Boonta Eve Podracing epic event, you get a 16 Force swing instead. With 4 ability, she is a no-brainer to any Dark Side deck that battles or relies on main characters. Her game text is interesting since it will depend on the opponent losing a character wielding a lightsaber at the same site. Not too common of an event if your opponent is using only Enhanced characters with built-in weapons, but you'll get a good benefit (i.e. higher immunity to attrition) should the opportunity arise. But enough about her game text. There are a variety of different deck types she will go straight into. For players who are big on playing the popular [[Jabba]]'s Palace effect, Scum And Villiany -- using the [[My Kind Of Scum / Fearless And Inventive{{!}}My Kind Of Scum]] objective (JPSD set) or [[Court Of The Vile Gangster / I Shall Enjoy Watching You Die{{!}}Court Of The Vile Gangster]] objective (Enhanced [[Jabba]]'s Palace set) -- Aurra will be a great addition to the rest of the aliens already in your deck. Even if you don't use Scum And Villany, Aurra is still useful in other decks if you like hunting for bounties. In [[Court Of The Vile Gangster / I Shall Enjoy Watching You Die{{!}}Court Of The Vile Gangster]], she gets forfeit +2 and bypasses [[Goo Nee Tay]]. Since Aurra is a bounty hunter, she will qualify for Agents Of The Black Sun (Reflections II/Expanded Universe set), which will benefit from having another bounty hunter. Combos: [[Aurra Sing]] + [[Quietly Observing]]: Why wait until the opponent just lost a character? Have Aurra sneak up on the opponent and just take it. Get your own glow stick. Petersenhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/small/blizzardscout1.html My favorite Dark Card. Enough said. Well, that would not make much of a card extra, would it? What combat vehicle is a staple of nearly every dark deck: the "Chicken Walker"! Take a look at the finalists decks from the 1997 World Championships, the mighty [[Blizzard Scout 1]] makes an appearance in both decks. Let's dissect this beauty. The [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is the AT-ST which made an extremely brief sprint across the screen during the Empire Strikes Back. What they didn't tell you in the movie was that [[Darth Vader]] was being whisked to the Echo [[Cloud City: East Platform (Docking Bay){{!}}Docking Bay]], and, by the way, he trampled [[Major Bren Derlin]] on his way in to the hangar (Sorry Mr. Claven) [You see, [[Major Bren Derlin]] was talking to [[2-1B (Too-Onebee){{!}}2-1B]] about this snowman who was the spitting image of Richard Nixon.... TRAMPLE]. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is the prototype of the Imperial's AT-ST cards which will come in Return of the Jedi expansions. This unique walker boasts everything you look for in a card. The Chicken Walker (named as such for its awkward look) is a natural in the mountains of [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] ([[Hoth: Mountains (6th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Mountains]], the [[Hoth: Mountains (6th Marker){{!}}6th Marker]]), where it deploys for 2 and has power 4, a great ratio. But wait, let's take a very typical game situation, [[Darth Vader]] is at the Defensive Perimeter waving his lightsaber at [[Commander Luke Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]] and Captain [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]]. Although they are out of sagacious gifts from the mentor or witty comments about not getting cocky (see the chicken theme), they decide to pick on our poor Dark Lord and initiate a battle. Well, Mr. [[Grand Moff Tarkin{{!}}Tarkin]] just hops aboard his [[Blizzard Scout 1]] and reacts all the way over to join his comrade in arms. This interlude brings up the real benefits of [[Blizzard Scout 1]]. First, it boasts a landspeed of 3, the ability to react, a permanent pilot and a slot to fill with a pilot -- a great package deal. Remember there are several 3 ability Dark Side Pilots out there. Second, just look at that destiny, a 4! Perfect to keep your average destiny up, and pulling one of these as destiny for [[Trample]] will squash all of those pesky Light Side spies. (OK OK, if Obi, [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]], [[Princess Leia]], [[BoShek]] or [[Yoda]] pull off [[Plastoid Armor]] and get [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] it will miss, but don't get technical with me!) Third, the walker is forfeit 5, a great way to soak up damage (just remember to lose the pilot first). Finally, there is also an S-comp link for good measure. Drawbacks. That is a tough one with the mighty Chicken Walker. But there are a couple. This walker does not have any immunity to attrition, despite its 4 armor rating. The other drawback is more of a reminder, [[Blizzard Scout 1]] does not count towards [[Walker Garrison]] as it is not an AT-AT. Forget that arrogant [[General Veers]] in his hulking [[Blizzard 1]], live life on the edge, blaze across the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] tundra in search of rebels to trample under foot with the all-powerful Chicken Waaaaalker! CARD COMBOS: [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Admiral Motti]] + Snowtroopers (at other locations) = Keep your leader on the move to respond to battles. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Trample]] = Rebel Spies in the Lost Pile. [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Boba Fett]] + [[Trample]] vs. [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]] = Blizzard Scout 1 + [[Boba Fett]] vs. [[Han Solo]] (could have saved the imperials a lot on bribing [[Lando Calrissian (Dark){{!}}Lando Calrissian]]). [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] Sites = With the vast number of [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] Sites, [[Blizzard Scout 1]] is your all-purpose scout combat vehicle! |combos=* [[Blizzard Scout 1]] + [[Admiral Motti]] + Snowtroopers (at other locations).[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Blizzard%20Scout%201 Scomp: Blizzard Scout 1]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). This unwavering devotion is represented by [[Maul]]'s unique icon, which is neither alien nor Imperial. [[Maul]]'s high deploy cost is comfortably offset by the reduced deploy to [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]], and is reduced even further if he deploys to the [[Tatooine: Hutt Trade Route (Desert){{!}}Desert]] Landing Site. [[Maul]]'s built-in dueling text seems risky with both players drawing the same number of destiny, but adding a duel destiny with a card like [[Focused Attack]] and setting up a high destiny draw with [[Maul's Electrobinoculars]] can quickly swing the duel in the Dark Jedi's favor. Of course, [[Maul]] is incredibly focused thanks to his thirst for revenge against the Jedi. As a result, most characters that aren't Force Attuned are beneath his notice. This is reflected in his gametext that kicks in if none of the Light Side characters at his location have ability of 4 or greater. At such a location, the Light Side's total ability is zero. In other words, the Light Side has no presence at this location, and thus cannot battle or be battled. In addition, it means that the Light Side will need to come up with an ability 4 or higher character in order to block [[Maul]]'s Force drains. Meanwhile, [[Maul]] with his Lightsaber and [[Sniper]] can gradually whittle away the Light Side's characters at his site. '''Virtual Legacy''' — [[Coruscant: Jedi Council Chamber (V)]] (1250_72) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Light Location: Coruscant: Jedi Council Chamber, Coruscant, R |strategy=By Doug Taylorhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/coruscant/light/small/coruscantjedicouncilchamber.html It's been 5 years since the game has seen the introduction of a 3/0 location. Back in 1996, the Dark Side got the [[Death Star (Special Edition){{!}}Death Star]] system in [[A New Hope]]. Now, the Light Side gets the first 3/0 site to balance things out. Any location that is so incredible for generating Force serves as a two-edged sword and poses a great danger for the person playing it. One must be extremely cautious to not allow it to fall into enemy hands, lest those 3 icons of Force-generating goodness be turned into a painful Force drain of 3 each turn. Fortunately, this new Light side mega-Force engine is custom-built to be the staging ground for the powerful and mysterious Jedi Council. Most of the Council members are completely immune to attrition there, and many cannot deploy anywhere else. Many of the strongest mechanics of these members (like those of [[Mace Windu]] and [[Depa Billaba]]) function only when that Jedi Master is contemplating the universe from within the sacred chambers. Another great feature of this locale is the ability to "download" [[Yoda, Senior Council Member]], who can then act to disperse your Jedi around the galaxy and augment your forces elsewhere. Combos: Use the Council Chamber as your "other [E1] location" on the Senator Objective to start yourself out with 4 Force icons while giving your opponent only 1. Card Size | 63x88mm |} '''Death Star II''' is the 25th expansion of Star Wars CCG, published by Decipher on 19 July 2000. It has 182 black-bordered cards, 91 per side.[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/deathstar2/light/index.html Death Star II Light Side card list], decipher.com (Wayback, 11 June 2002)[https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/deathstar2/dark/index.html Death Star II Dark Side card list], decipher.com (Wayback, 11 June 2002) They are 2 ultra rares ([[Luke Skywalker, Jedi Knight]] and [[Emperor Palpatine]]), 78 rares, 50 uncommons and 50 commons. Two exclusive rares, [[Admiral Ackbar]] and [[Admiral Piett]], came only in starters. It covers the Battle of Endor and the second Death Star. Packs have 11 cards (7 commons, 3 uncommons, 1 rare or ultra rare), MSRP $3.29, 36 per box. Starter decks have 60 cards, MSRP $10.95, 12 per box (6 per side). Starter decks also include 55 reprint fixed cards with a 2000 copyright. See [[Death Star II Light Side Starter Deck]] and [[Death Star II Dark Side Starter Deck]].[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2] Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009141805/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive] == Packaging == {| class="wikitable" style="background:transparent; border:none;" |- style="background:transparent; border:none; vertical-align:bottom;" | style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:DS2-Limited-display.png|260px|Death Star II display]]

''Rule book'' |} == Memorabilia == Decipher issued a four-panel poster (~32″ × 10.5″) for every expansion from Premiere through Death Star II. Death Star II's reverse is the expansion card list plus a pre-constructed deck list. Yeah, I couldn't believe it either. The Sakiyan bounty hunter is an underused powerhouse, for fairly obvious reasons. Ability = 4 is one big reason: any card that draws battle destiny on its own speaks for itself. Add to that [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]'s immunity to attrition < 3, and you've got a guy who can draw his own destiny AND potentially avoid falling victim to the attrition of his enemies. Can you think of any other characters with such abilities? Do the names [[Darth Vader]], [[Luke Skywalker]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], or [[Princess Leia]] ring a bell? Djas does appear to have one glaring weakness upon first glance: Power = 1, but take another look at his game text: Power +1 for each DS icon present, +2 under "nighttime conditions." Ouch...drop [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]] at any DS location with two DS icons, and he's Power = 3. Add a [[Presence Of The Force]], and he's Power = 4. Make that DS location the [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]], and he's Power = 5. Play [[Sunsdown]] on [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]]...forget about it...Power = 8...my man is ragin': "The [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] is MY house!!!" But it doesn't end there: this guy is rife with combo potential. Let's go back to his Ability = 4. Not only can he utilize the Dark Jedi abilities of [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Sense]] and [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] with some proficiency, but also: can you say, "[[Weapon Levitation]]?" That's right: "I'll take that lightsaber, Mr. [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Kenobi]]." What's that? You say you don't use [[Weapon Levitation]]? (Well, you should!) Just give Djas (a warrior, by the way) his own [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber]]...only 3 Force to deploy and target (much less than most DS characters), and he has as much chance to hit Rebels and their co-conspirators as [[Lord Vader]] himself. The lightsaber combos that follow go without saying ([[All Too Easy]], [[Disarmed (Dark){{!}}Disarmed]], [[You Are Beaten]], etc., etc.). Also, want to add a little extra attrition to your damage with [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]? Try [[Res Luk Ra'auf]], adding a battle destiny for a bounty hunter defending alone, giving Djas and his Ability = 4 not one, but TWO battle destiny draws. This list goes on, but you get the picture...[[Djas Puhr]], Sakiyan bounty hunter, ROCKS. He is a must in most DS ground decks and can really show his stuff when the LS spreads their forces thin to force drain and leaves characters with less than Ability = 4 at a site. Next time you need some hired ground muscle (and one heck of a tracker), call on [[Djas Puhr{{!}}Puhr]]. Combos: Djas + [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] + [[Presence Of The Force]] = Power of 5, Immunity to Attrition < 3, and a destiny draw. Djas + [[Weapon Levitation]] = one less unique LS lightsaber to worry about...and one more for you to USE. Djas + [[Res Luk Ra'auf]] = 2 battle destiny. '''Decipher Errata''' — [[Dr. Evazan (Errata)]] (1_172) |sources=* [[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Glossary Version 2.0]] (November 1998) * Printed face: [[Dr. Evazan]] |strategy=By Tom Lischkehttps://web.archive.org/web/20001010190651/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/drevazan.html Dark Side Rare 2 [[Dr. Evazan]](DE) is an absolute must in any Dark Side(DS) weapons deck. First, the combination of pilot and warrior, along with [[Dr. Evazan{{!}}Evazan]]'s game text, make DE one of the three best aliens for the DS, along with [[Djas Puhr]] and [[Dannik Jerriko]]. DE's ability to cause a hit or [[Disarmed (Dark){{!}}Disarmed]] character to be immediately lost can change the results of a battle he is in considerably, often depriving the LS player of a battle destiny draw. DE is ideal for a DS [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] ground deck, with a heavy emphasis on powerful weapons, such as [[Blaster]] Rifles and Dark Jedi Lightsabers. With careful deck design, such as the inclusion of some high destiny effects and interrupts to boost weapon destiny draws, DE can become a keystone for a deck. Some helpful effects and interrupts for the doctor and friends which also have high destiny numbers are [[Disarmed (Dark){{!}}Disarmed]] (5), [[It's Worse]] (6), [[Precise Attack]] (4), [[Trooper Charge]] (6), [[Lone Warrior]] (4), [[Besieged]] (5), Oo-ta Go-ta [[Han Solo{{!}}Solo]] (5), and [[Tentacle]] (5). Some of the key locations for a DE deck are [[Death Star]]:Detention Block Corridor and [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]]:Lars Moisture Farm, which allow the DS player to add one to each weapon destiny draw. DE and his associate, [[Ponda Baba]], are both power plus one at both [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]]:[[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] and [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]]:Mos Eisley. Add a few high forfeit, low deploy cost warriors to protect the doctor from attrition, and turn him loose on the sands of [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]]. Cards to watch out for: All six of the seekers. Combos: DE + [[Disarmed (Dark){{!}}Disarmed]] + Any character weapon. Deploy DE and a weapon at the site of any Light character packing a weapon. Play [[Disarmed (Dark){{!}}Disarmed]] on the character during the LS player's control phase, and even [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Obi-Wan's Lightsaber]] are immediately lost. A nice feature of this combo is that it is immune to [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] or any other counter and does not require a destiny draw to execute. DE + [[Dannik Jerriko]] + Weapon. During a battle, hit a character with a weapon, have DE operate on the character, and then have Dannik eat his soup. This instantly swings the power total in the battle by the ability plus power of the LS character. Mark Tuttle, Decipher Netrep, gets credit for this one. Common/Uncommon Combo: DE + [[Ponda Baba]] + 2 Imperial Blasters + [[Precise Attack]]. [[Dr. Evazan{{!}}Evazan]] just feels more comfortable with his cohort who 'doesn't like you either.' This gruesome twosome has a power of six, or eight at either DS [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] or Mos Eisley. Give them both Imperial Blasters and play a [[Precise Attack]], and one LS character of your choice probably will not walk away from the confrontation. Make your opponent cringe Combo: DE + [[Jawa (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Jawa]] + [[Utinni! (Dark){{!}}Utinni!]] + [[Kessel Run]]. Have one of your Jawas catch a ship to [[Kessel (Dark){{!}}Kessel]]. Use [[Utinni! (Dark){{!}}Utinni!]] to steal [[Kessel Run]] into your hand, and then have DE make the run using his Smuggler attribute. '''Decipher (Revised)''' — [[General Veers (Revised)]] (53_87) |sources=* [[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] (November 1998) * Printed face: [[General Veers]] |strategy=By Gregg Keefer, Gold 4https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/hoth/dark/small/generalveers.html [[General Veers]] is one bad dude. How many people out there can face [[Darth Vader]], nose to breathing apparatus, without flinching? Aside from hispersonal charm and charisma his card is stacked with tons of useful abilitiesthat will add to your Dark Side deck and make those rebels quake with fear! For 3 Force you get 3 power and 3 ability as well as [[Red Leader{{!}}Leader]] ability. Add to that the fact that he is a Warrior and a Pilot and you have a useful, do-it-all character that works well in practically any deck strategy. But that's notall, this guy is the bomb. His pilot text carries added bonuses if you use him on combat vehicles. He adds 3 to the power of any combat vehicle which can make any Walker a nightmare to be reckoned with. Put him on the [[Imperial Walker]] from the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] 2 player game[, with its permanent pilot of ability 1, and you have 7 power and a battle destiny draw for only 7 Force. Put him on [[Blizzard 1]] and [[Veers]] commands a staggering 10 power, immunity to attrition less than 4 and a battle destiny draw all by himself ! The mighty General also adds 1 to armor on this Walker making it that much harder for those pesky Snowspeeders to take him down with their puny weapons. Bah, annoying gadflies! He's great on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] but he can really make trouble for those rebels at Cloud Sectors too. Put him on a [[Cloud Car (Dark){{!}}Cloud Car]] (a combat vehicle) at a Cloud Sector and you are looking at 6 power and a battle destiny draw for only 5 Force. Combine this with some Tibanna Gas Miners on the ground to add to your Force drain at the sector. If it's a Light Side cloud sector you're controlling you'll drain for 2, plus the Miner bonus. Nasty. He's also power plus one at the same site as that bumbling freebie [[Admiral Ozzel]] and they'll bring you 7 power (8 on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]) plus a battle destiny for only 3 Force. Ozzel was born to be forfeited to attrition, leaving [[Veers]] to fight again another day. Should the unthinkable happen and [[Veers]] is defeated, his better than average forfeit of 5 will usually eat up even a high single destiny in attrition. General Maximillian [[Veers]]' great abilities have won him the admiration of the Empire. He is yours to command. Call it sentiment, a reminder of that favorite movie scene when [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]] gives [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]] his father's lightsaber, and introduces us to this elegant weapon. [[Gift Of The Mentor]] is an elegant weapon, too. If [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]] finds himself in battle together with either of his mentors, [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]] or [[Yoda]], it allows the Light Side to draw two additional battle destiny. Three battle destiny are usually enough to sweep away the Dark Side characters opposing these Jedi. The secondary use, allowing the player to use 1 Force to search the Reserve Deck for any lightsaber, is key in many decks that require a fast start and Force drain bonuses from lightsabers. It is also nice to have a card in your deck that cuts down on the use of duplicate copies of [[Obi-Wan's Lightsaber]] or [[Anakin's Lightsaber]]. [[Gift Of The Mentor]] is a lost interrupt, but has a great destiny of 5. It can be Sensed, but this can be anticipated and prevented by [[Control]]. '''Virtual Modern Errata''' — [[Greedo (V) (Errata)]] (204_42) — current |sources=* Original printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080512224452/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/greedo.html Greedo], [[Decipher]] (archived 12 May 2008). * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Character: Greedo, A New Hope, R1 |strategy=By Tom Landyhttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/greedo.html [[Greedo]] isn't the greatest alien. In fact, nearly everybody says that his card isn't even worth space in a deck. But, in some cases, he can really be useful. At a deploy cost of one, this bounty hunter's power is two, his ability is one, his destiny is two, but his forfeit is only a half. [[Greedo]] also possesses a special ability which allows him to "threaten" Smugglers. His game text says: " During opponent's control phase, may "threaten" one smuggler at same site. Opponent may use all force pile cards to cancel "threat", allowing you to activate the same amount. Otherwise, draw destiny. If destiny plus [[Greedo]]'s ability is >6, smuggler is lost." Now I know what you are thinking. "Why would anyone use [[Greedo]]? His forfeit stinks, and to kill a smuggler, the destiny must be a six!" While all of this is true, there are always ways to improve things. For instance, to improve his forfeit, keep him around the dark side's [[Tatooine: Mos Eisley (Dark){{!}}Tatooine: Mos Eisley]]. Here, [[Greedo]]'s forfeit would get a plus one bonus, and his power would be three. Another quick way to boost his forfeit is to slap a [[Stormtrooper Utility Belt]] around his waist. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit and power would both get a plus one bonus, but if he was on the [[Death Star]], the bonus would be plus two. Now, a forfeit of two and a half isn't bad. If you have a lot of destinies of six in your deck, you will be able to "threaten" major smugglers like [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]], [[Chewbacca]], and even [[Wedge Antilles]] easily if you have certain cards that will help you. An [[Electrobinoculars]] would be ideal to locate destinies of six, if only the dark side had this device. So, use [[Reegesk]], [[Tonnika Sisters]] or any other way to steal them from your opponent. [[Electrobinoculars]] is a very popular and powerful card, so you don't have to really worry about your opponent not having them. Another good way to find destinies that you need is with [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]]. When at a scomp link, [[R2-Q2 (Artoo-Kyootoo){{!}}R2-Q2]] enables you to peek at the top three cards of your reserve deck during your draw phase for one force. By knowing what your destiny is, even if it isn't a six, you can still bluff because your opponent won't know if you are lying or not. [[Greedo]]'s forfeit value and special ability to "threaten" smugglers aren't great, but when combined with certain cards it can really be helpful. |pulled_by=* [[Double Back]]Lookup: [https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Greedo Scomp: Greedo]. {{Card |title=I Did It! |card_uid=11_25o |image=Tat-L-ididit-decipher-archive.jpg |hires_image=Tat-L-ididit-hires.webp |side=Light |type=Epic Event |set=Tatooine |publisher=[[Decipher]] |era=[[Decipher era]] |rarity=R |rarity_link=Rarity#Rare |uniqueness=Unique |destiny=0 |version_label=printed |set_band=Decipher |prev=I Can't Believe He's Gone |next=Jar Jar Binks |game_text=Deploy on table if you've won a Podrace. Once per game, may place Boonta Eve Podrace out of play to retrieve 4 Force. If you occupy a battleground site and a battleground system, once during each of your control phases may take the bottom card of your Lost Pile and place it on top of your Force Pile. At the end of opponent's turn opponent must lose 2 Force or place their Force Pile onto their Used Pile. |printings='''Decipher''' — '''this page''' (11_25o)
'''PC Errata''' — [[I Did It! (PC Errata)]] (11_25) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Light Epic Event: I Did It!, Tatooine, R |strategy=By Martin Arlthttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/tatooine/light/small/ididit.html So, your deck's podracing theme has played itself out, and you're left with a copy of [[Boonta Eve Podrace]] sitting on the table. It's not doing anything. The race is over, the concessions stands have closed, the holo-broadcasting crews have gone home, and the maintenance droids are busy clearing away the barely recognizable remains of several podracers. As is often the case with Epic Events, [[Boonta Eve Podrace]] does its thing, and then is forgotten. But the Light Side gets a second Epic Event in [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]]: [[I Did It!]] This card builds on your success with [[Boonta Eve Podrace]]. In fact, these two cards together are almost like the two sides of an Objective. [[I Did It!]] can be deployed after you won a podrace. You can place that now-useless [[Boonta Eve Podrace]] out of play to retrieve 4 force. In addition to this one-time benefit, you have several very tasty long-term bonuses. First, while you occupy a battleground site and a battleground system, you can place the bottom card of your Lost Pile onto your Force Pile. In one action, you not only retrieve a Force, but you also increase your Force activation. The second benefit is one that is likely to cause the Dark Side endless trouble. At the end of his turn, your opponent must choose to lose 2 Force or place his Force pile into his Used pile. This wreaks havoc in several ways. For one, the Dark Side will be hard pressed to save up Force to use during your turn, making it difficult to react, fire weapons that have a firing cost, and play certain Interrupts. In addition, the Dark Side player will find itself having to carefully manage his activation. If he has Force left over at the end of his turn, and he chooses to replace the cards in his Used Pile, he will have to work a little harder to track destinies. [[I Did It!]] is a powerful card that will be invaluable in building on your successes in racing. It is likely that it will be a key card in making podracing a key strategy in some areas, rather than just an occasional side strategy. |combos=* [[I Did It!]] + [[Draw Their Fire]] If your opponent wants to be able to use any Interrupt in a battle you initiate, they will have to lose 2 Force each turn (provided you meet the conditions on [[I Did It!]]). (Psychobabble)[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=I%20Did%20It%21 Scomp: I Did It!]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020174249/https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json Internet Archive] |rulings=* A Force Pile can be placed onto a Used Pile even if one or both piles are empty. * Light can only place their own copy of [[Boonta Eve Podrace]] out of play, not the opponent's copy. |pulled_by=* [[Anakin's Podracer]] |underlying_card_for=* [[Anakin Skywalker, Junkyard Slave]] |has_refs=1 }}

No cool double-bladed lightsaber? Relax. This is the [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] expansion, remember? [[Maul]] just used a single-bladed version in this part of the movie. As such, this weapon follows the format established by other unique lightsaber cards, with one notable exception. When [[Maul]] is using this weapon, it cannot be stolen. This simple bit of gametext protects [[Maul's Lightsaber]] from annoying interrupts like [[Weapon Levitation]], that can result in the Dark Side suddenly finding itself weaponless in a battle. In addition, [[Maul]] can make excellent use of his weapon. [[Maul]] can effectively ignore the presence of Light Side characters of ability less than 4. This means he can Force drain while at their site, using [[Maul's Lightsaber]] to add 1 to the Force drain. He can also use cards like [[Sniper]] to take pot-shots at those poor, low-ability characters, gradually reducing their numbers at his site. Light Side alien swarm decks will want to avoid this armed Dark Jedi as much as possible. Finally, like other lightsabers, [[Maul's Lightsaber]] gets two weapons destiny draws, making it easier to hit even high-ability characters like [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]] and Qui-Gon. [[Maul]] also has the advantage of using [[Maul's Electrobinoculars]] to rig a high destiny draw, practically guaranteeing a hit against even a Jedi Master if you take the time! |pulled_by=* [[I Will Finish What You Started]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Maul%27s%20Lightsaber Scomp: Maul's Lightsaber]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). Loser (lowest total) is lost. |printings='''Decipher''' — '''this page''' (12_153) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Interrupt: Maul Strikes, Coruscant, R |strategy=By [mailto:joea@decipher.com Joe Alread, Decipher Game Designer]https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/coruscant/dark/small/maulstrikes.html The biggest complaint about [[Darth Maul]] from [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] was that his support cards were a bit weak when compared to [[Darth Vader]] or [[Ben Kenobi]]. Some things just take time, and [[Maul]] can happily take a big step up the main character chain with [[Maul Strikes]]. The three uses this card has are all extremely powerful. When you draw this card, one of its uses will almost certainly be needed immediately. Light Side players have been able to pull Lightsabers out of their decks for years with [[Gift Of The Mentor]], and now [[Maul Strikes]] allows the Dark Side to finally have their turn at this great ability. Another minor weakness of the [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] persona of [[Darth Maul]] was that his ability to duel was a bit restricted, since he had to essentially survive an entire turn before he had the chance to duel anybody. With [[Maul Strikes]], however, the Sith Lord can bypass that restriction, and duel at any time by simply playing this interrupt. And finally, if you're looking for just some good old beatdown, [[Maul]] can add battle destiny with this card too. Instead of just dueling Qui-Gon and making him lost, why not battle him, cut him, and draw three battle destiny as well? The answer is simple. |pulls=* [[Dark Jedi Lightsaber]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Maul%20Strikes Scomp: Maul Strikes]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). [[Obi-Wan Kenobi, Padawan Learner]] provides a simple lesson for how the problem can be avoided altogether. The youthful [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] Expansion version of Obi-wan has a higher power than his Classic Trilogy versions. As a result, he cannot be replaced by those versions via persona replacement. Similarly, his ability is lower than those versions, meaning that the older [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Kenobi]] cannot be replaced with the younger one. This is a simple mechanic with no new persona rules to learn, just the use of an already-established rule. As the expansion title suggests, young Obi-wan is strongly linked to [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] in his usefulness. First, he receives a generous deploy bonus to [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] that allows him to deploy for a pittance of 4 Force. Not bad for a character with 6 power and 5 ability, plus a healthy amount of immunity to attrition. But what makes our young Padawan really interesting is his 'teleporting' gametext. When the Dark Side player initiates a battle at a related [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] site, Obi-wan can relocate to the battle for 2 Force, giving the Light Side an added power boost in the battle, not to mention the chance to hit a character if Obi-wan is carrying his lightsaber. The Dark Side will have to carefully consider when and where to battle on [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] in order to effectively deal with the teleporting Jedi hit-man. And getting young Obi-wan into play is helped by the gametext of [[Padmé Naberrie]], who lets [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Kenobi]] deploy from the Reserve Deck. Obi-wan [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Kenobi]], Padawan Learner continues the tradition of great personae of [[Ben Kenobi]]. '''Decipher Errata''' — [[Presence Of The Force (Errata)]] (1_227) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/index.html Premiere Dark Side card list] at Decipher.com (archive, 11 June 2002) * Original printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020804005247/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/presenceoftheforce.html Presence Of The Force], [[Decipher]] (archived 4 August 2002). * Printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020804005247/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/images/presenceoftheforce.gif Decipher.com card image] (Wayback copy of decipher.com/starwars/cardlists) |strategy=By Justin Pakeshttps://web.archive.org/web/20001010191601/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/presenceoftheforce.html Imagine my dismay as I browsed the voluminous libraries of Deciphers card lists to discover that one of my favourite (proper English spelling there... :) cards was sans card extra. The often acronymed, PotF. So lets see if I can add anything to even that score. Being a Premiere card, the old hands amongst you may not find anything new here, but then again, maybe a refresher is in order. The card adds one red and one blue Force icon to whatever location you deploy it. A sabre for me, and a sabre for you. The deploy is zero as are the deployment restrictions. It's a two dot card, but remember that "cumulativity" stops you gaining any benefits from two copies at the same location. The wonderous thing about this card is it's elegant simplicity but amazing versatility. One use of the card is a boon to the early game. It is an extra Force activated. And in that frustrating game where the only time you see your locations is as destiny draws, that extra one can be vital. The most obvious offensive use of this card is immediately apparent, a bigger drain at a location, preferably one you already securely control! Lovely for you, added headache for your opponent! And never forget that it is *any* location. Handy if your opponent forgot to stock Cloud Cars and your trying to boost the benefit of your cloud superiority! "Just another drain bonus" some of you are saying, I can get that with a sabre! But with the advent of [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]], the true value of a PotF used in this way was realised. Being an extra icon, and NOT a drain bonus (such as +1 to Force Drains) it is immune to that 'Bane of the Drain', [[Great Warrior]] (Jedi Test #1). The alternate use is a little more subtle. At a location where you have no force icons, this card is better than a spy. Sure, it can't go undercover, but it won't get snipered by the first weapon that comes along either. That extra icon allows you normal deploy, and is like the front door key to many LS starting locations. E.g. Massasi [[Hoth: Echo Command Center (War Room){{!}}War Room]], Obi's Hut, [[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] Echo Base Command Centre (before the shields go up), or even LS [[Dantooine (Dark){{!}}Dantooine]]. If you can get the power down you need to hold them, that makes for a big early drain. If you have it in hand really early, it can be your only hope against those irritating LS decks that revolve your starting location early depriving you of force. Even better, allow yourself to get to that LS Big One and cancel that darned Asteroid Sanctuary. There are also a few more esoteric uses. A couple of cards are concerned with the number of icons at a location. [[Djas Puhr]], [[Feltipern Trevagg]], or even [[Commence Primary Ignition]] for a little added destruction. I would also say Braniac, but when it comes to that sort of mathematical proficiency, I'm a weak-minded fool. ;) "The perfect all round card!" I hear you now exclaim. Surely there's a catch! And indeed there is. But to me, the quality that makes this a *great* card is how it is a double-edged sabre if you use it without thinking. Very appopriate when you consider the picture on the card. Play it early, and you could be giving your opponent much needed Force activation. Put it on a location you cannot hold, and you may well feel the sting of the extra drain. Without proper planninng and situational analysis, many of the benefits could end up benefitting the Light Side. This tool belongs to the thinking player. And beware the counters too. Cloud City's Clash Of Sabres will cancel it outright. [[Alter (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Alter]] has the same effect, but there's plenty of counter-counter's to that. And most irritating of all is [[I Have A Bad Feeling About This]] which LS can use to retarget it to a location they control (e.g. [[Dagobah Limited|Dagobah]]!). I always recommend the multi-function [[Bad Feeling Have I]] to take care of that problem. Combos: How can you list combos for something that can be used almost anywhere, anytime? Obvious => PotF + LS Obi's Hut + your characters controlling it with a Vaders sabre and a Dark Jedi Sabre = drain of 6. Favourite => PotF + DS Mos Eisley + [[Sunsdown]] + [[Djas Puhr]] = An alien who even alone is Power 8, Ability 4, Forfeit 5, Immune To Attrition < 3, draws destiny, and gets an extra destiny worth of power! Even [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] would quietly thank the Emperor that he's on the right side of that behemoth! For icing on the attrition cake, add [[Lone Warrior]] + [[Moment Of Triumph]], stir vigourously, and draw 2 extra destiny's. |combos=* [[Presence Of The Force]] + [[Endor Shield (V)]] + [[Endor (expansion)|Endor]] Three Force icons for you, none for the Light Side. '''Decipher Errata''' — [[Revolution (Errata)]] (1_62) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20020611184117/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/light/index.html Premiere Light Side card list] at Decipher.com (archive, 11 June 2002) * Original printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020804005247/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/light/small/revolution.html Revolution], [[Decipher]] (archived 4 August 2002). * Printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20020804005247/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/light/images/revolution.gif Decipher.com card image] (Wayback copy of decipher.com/starwars/cardlists) |strategy=By Jim Van Fleet, RED 15https://web.archive.org/web/20020803212054/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/light/small/revolution.html [[Revolution]]. Its what the Rebel Alliance is all about! This Effect from the Premiere Edition has endured, and even grown in popularity through all the game expansions. Many players find it an indispensable tool in the battle to overthrow the Empire. A list of the benefits of [[Revolution]]: 1) it can be deployed on any location (except the [[Death Star]]) 2) it Revolves (switches) not only the game text, but also the Force icons at that location, 3) although it is not cumulative, there is no limit to how many [[Revolution]] cards can be in play. When the Premiere Edition stood alone, [[Revolution]] was used most often as a way to increase Light Side Force drains. Played on [[Tatooine: Obi-Wan's Hut]], it created an easy Force drain of 3. This strategy is still prevalent, but now many players rely on [[Revolution]] at [[Dagobah: Yoda's Hut]] to create a Force drain that is difficult to counter. Equally important is the strategy of using [[Revolution]] to take away game text and Force icons from the Dark Side. Deploying a couple of Revolutions early in the game can cripple Dark Side ground-based decks such as [[Walker Garrison]] or [[Tatooine (expansion)|Tatooine]] drain, by denying them both Force generation and Force drain bonuses. [[Revolution]] has a destiny of 3, pretty average, and a fairly high deploy cost of 3. The main drawbacks of this card are the new cards that Decipher has created, which specifically counteract the powerful effects of [[Revolution]]. The Light Side player must be prepared with multiple [[Sense]] and [[Control]] cards to defend [[Revolution]] against [[Evader]] or [[Surprise]] , and may find it impossible to counter the very popular [[Imperial Decree]]. On a positive note, [[Revolution]] is not cancelled by [[Imperial Decree]], just "ignored." Late in a game, if the Light Side prevails and the conditions for [[Imperial Decree]] cannot be met, the Dark Side will suffer the effects of [[Revolution]] again! I like to call him the General Zod of SWCCG. If you plan to base your deck around the Galactic Senate, or if you just want to mop the floor with those weenie Dark Side Senators for laughs, [[Supreme Chancellor Valorum]] is your man. With a hefty 5 Politics, Valorum has the highest concentration of political power in the game. Even better, Valorum has excellent stats outside of the Senate, with 4 Ability (all the better to draw battle destiny when alone at the Senate) and a whopping 7 Forfeit. Top it all off with a multiple-use-friendly 3 Destiny, and the Supreme Chancellor's a shoe-in for any deck. But it's his skill in the Senate that makes Valorum a top choice for any deck. While in a Senate majority, he's a one-man [[Grand Moff Tarkin{{!}}Tarkin]], with the power to cancel an opponent's battle destiny at any site, anywhere, any time, for only 1 Force. That's what I like to call sledgehammer politics. And it's all from the safety of the Galactic Senate, where Walkers and Sith Lords are strictly pooh-poohed. Of course, Valorum's power comes with a price. You remember all those "baseless" accusations we heard about in the movie? Well, they're back with a vengeance. As long as your opponent has Force to spend, he can reduce Valorum's Politics infinitely. While this doesn't hinder Valorum when it comes to guerilla "votes" in the Senate, it does make controlling the Senate with him alone a risky proposition. Be prepared to back him up with other political figures, like [[Queen Amidala]]... or a certain future Supreme Chancellor... Combos: cancel two battle destiny? I'm there! POWER 1 Protocol Droid If in a battle with Shmi at a site, once per battle may place top card of your Used Pile on top of your Reserve Deck. Once per turn may place a card from hand into your Used Pile to draw top card from Reserve Deck. DEPLOY 2 FORFEIT 3 The Episode I version of [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}Threepio]] is a great card for anyone who likes to have full control over their deck. [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}Threepio]] shares [[Mirax Terrik]]'s ability to circulate high destiny cards back into your deck and replace them with new cards from the Reserve Deck. What's even nicer about [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}Threepio]]'s ability is that, unlike Mirax, his ability can be used for free, and instead of placing the card on the bottom of the Used Pile, he places it on the top of the Used Pile for easier tracking when your Reserve Deck is larger. The other nice thing about [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}Threepio]]'s ability to place a high destiny card on top of your Used Pile is that if he's in a battle with Shmi, he can then take that high destiny card and place it on top of your Reserve Deck, ensuring a nice pull for weapon or battle destiny. And since Shmi can download [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}Threepio]] right out of the Reserve Deck, the odds of you having them in a battle together are pretty good. The fact that this is a persona of [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}C-3PO]] also has enormous benefits. Because most versions of [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}C-3PO]] have only been strong in specialized decks, many of his support cards are quite powerful. For example, [[Were You Looking For Me?]] is a handy 5 Destiny Used Interrupt that allows you to pull [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}Threepio]] and/or another protocol droid (like [[R-3PO (Ar-Threepio){{!}}R-3PO]]) from your Reserve Deck. You can also use the same Interrupt as a Lost Interrupt to either retrieve [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}Threepio]] from the Lost Pile or to add a battle destiny when [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}Threepio]] is helping his friends out in battle (two battle destiny if he happens to have a few furry friends with him). Unlike most "back" cards, this card is very appealing because it's recyclable, free, high destiny, and has the battle destiny bonus. There are tons of other [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}C-3PO]] suppport cards, including the ever-popular [[How Did We Get Into This Mess?]], but one of my favorites is [[Artoo, I Have A Bad Feeling About This]], which has three different uses, the best of which allows you to squash your opponent's battle destiny completely if both [[Artoo (Jabba's Palace){{!}}Artoo]] and [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}C-3PO]] are together in battle. Put Shmi, [[Artoo (Jabba's Palace){{!}}Artoo]] and [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}Threepio]] together in a battle, and with the right support cards you can really put the hurt on the Dark Side.https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/tatooine/light/small/threepiowithhispartsshow.html |combos=* [[Threepio With His Parts Showing]] + [[Chewie With Blaster Rifle]] [[Chewie With Blaster Rifle]] adds one battle destiny if with [[C-3PO (See-Threepio){{!}}C-3PO]].[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Threepio%20With%20His%20Parts%20Showing Scomp: Threepio With His Parts Showing]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). For those who play the increasingly popular [[Walker Garrison]] deck, a [[Wampa]] offers some unique advantages. If the Dark Side has a [[Hoth: Wampa Cave (7th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Wampa Cave]] on the table, they can deploy this creature for free. If there are any non-droid characters elsewhere on [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]], the [[Wampa]] begins to move towards them. Dark Side characters can avoid the [[Wampa]] (and Ice Storms, and blasters, lightsabers and etc.) by staying in Imperial Walkers or Blizzard Walkers. Light Side characters may be more vulnerable to attack, even if they are at interior sites. The [[Wampa]] is full of surprises, and packs a powerful punch, as [[Commander Luke Skywalker]] discovered. A Dark Side player could arrange a destiny draw of 7, making this creature a hard-to-beat 10 power in an attack! Wampas can deploy under the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] shields, at locations without presence or even Force icons, wreaking havoc on an [[Echo Base Operations]] deck or a [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] numbers deck if it uses non-droid characters such as [[Wioslea]]! Finally, the [[Wampa]] has a unique ability: he may choose to send his victims to the [[Hoth: Wampa Cave (7th Marker){{!}}Hoth: Wampa Cave]] instead of the lost pile. Imagine a [[Wampa]] tearing through the [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]]: Echo Base Command Center, sending Light Side characters to the Cave one at a time, while the Dark Side sets up a welcoming committee of powerful characters in the Cave, guarded by Walkers with AT-AT Cannons at the exterior site just outside. Combo: , then a massive deployment to the [[Wampa]] Cave: Lots of punishment for the Light Side player, who can't move away, since his feet seem to have frozen into the ice! |combos=* [[Wampa]] + [[Cold Feet]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Wampa Scomp: Wampa]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). '''Virtual Legacy''' — [[You May Start Your Landing (V)]] (1282_3) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Effect: You May Start Your Landing, Tatooine, R |strategy=By Andrew Parkshttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/tatooine/dark/small/youmaystartyourlanding.html This card heralds the return of the almighty [[Walker Garrison]] deck. Being able to start this effect with [[Prepared Defenses]] is a great boost to this classic deck type. On your first turn, you can immediately go and grab the [[Hoth: Defensive Perimeter (3rd Marker) (Dark){{!}}3rd Marker]], which combined with the [[Hoth: Ice Plains (5th Marker){{!}}5th Marker]] gives you 4 red icons and a +1 Force Drain location, while the Light Side only gets one blue icon from you in the bargain. Plus, you are guaranteed to have a [[Walker Garrison]] in hand right from the get-go, so you are all set to drain like mad once you've got all your Walkers in position. The best part of this card, however, is its ability to deal direct damage just by occupying [[Hoth (Dark){{!}}Hoth]] marker sites with AT-ATs, which any self-respecting [[Walker Garrison]] deck has in abundance. If you choose [[No Escape]] as one of your starting effects, this direct damage will not be cancelled by Honor of the Jedi, which is a good thing since your force drains at non-battlegrounds will be negated by that powerful Light Side card. Be sure to pack a couple Presence of the Force to help turn those Marker Sites into battlegrounds and add to your drains in the bargain. For a third starting effect for this deck type, you probably want to start with [[Imperial Arrest Order]]. This will give a big boost to all your Walker pilots, and allow you to deploy the [[Hoth: Echo Docking Bay (Dark){{!}}Hoth: Echo Docking Bay]] right away, a great place to plop a Walker to help drain with [[Walker Garrison]]. Unfortunately, the [[Cloud City: East Platform (Docking Bay){{!}}Docking Bay]] isn't a Marker Site, but it's still a great battleground to drain at with your Walkers. An alternative starting effect is [[Imperial Decree]], which is pretty easy to keep active with this deck and which can really hurt those cowardly Rebels. |pulled_by=* [[Twi'lek Advisor]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=You%20May%20Start%20Your%20Landing Scomp: You May Start Your Landing]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec).
